short: Flamboyant monarch and Prince Regent whose extravagance defined the Regency era's culture.
full:
George IV spent nine years as Prince Regent before his accession in 1820, acting for his incapacitated father, George III. His reign was characterised by immense personal extravagance, cultural patronage, and a scandalous private life, including a highly public and damaging attempt to divorce his wife, Caroline of Brunswick, which severely undermined the monarchy's prestige.

Despite his unpopularity and political indolence, his era saw major artistic and architectural achievements, most notably the Royal Pavilion in Brighton and the extensive remodelling of Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle. Politically, his reign witnessed the grudging concession of Catholic Emancipation in 1829, a measure he fiercely resisted before capitulating to his ministers.
